hypotheses.text: Ectopia lentis (HP:0001083) is universally absent (0% penetrance) in molecularly verified SMAD2/LDS6 patients, serving as an absolute clinical counter-indicator that excludes LDS6 in favor of FBN1-related Marfan syndrome.
hypotheses.rationale: Classical diagnostic criteria and nosology for Loeys-Dietz syndrome maintain that ocular lens dislocation is unique to fibrillinopathies (Marfan syndrome) and strictly absent in TGF-beta vasculopathies, including LDS6. Proving whether true ectopia lentis ever occurs in confirmed SMAD2 pathogenic variant carriers will resolve whether presence of ectopia lentis has 100% negative predictive value for LDS6.

evidence.text: Absence of ectopia lentis in LDS is noted as a major distinguishing feature separating Loeys-Dietz syndrome from Marfan syndrome, while recognizing that too few SMAD2 mutation-positive cases have been reported to determine the full phenotypic boundaries.

hypotheses.text: Reported occurrences of ectopia lentis in aggregated Loeys-Dietz syndrome cohorts represent clinical misattribution or phenocopies (such as severe myopia or microspherophakia) rather than genuine zonular rupture/dislocation caused by SMAD2 mutations.
hypotheses.rationale: Large systematic reviews pooling hundreds of multi-database reports occasionally tabulate ectopia lentis in LDS cohorts; testing whether these rare exceptions withstand rigorous slit-lamp re-evaluation or represent dual diagnoses/diagnostic misclassifications will establish whether the exclusion dogma holds.

evidence.text: Comparative literature discussing Marfan syndrome and Loeys-Dietz syndrome emphasizes that higher probabilities of ectopia lentis distinguish MFS from LDS, even while both share progressive TGF-beta-mediated aortic root disease.

hypotheses.text: SMAD2-specific ocular pathology is restricted to non-zonular manifestations such as hypertelorism, strabismus, blue sclerae, and high myopia, with complete sparing of the ciliary zonule and lens position.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying the specific ocular profile of SMAD2 variant carriers will provide ophthalmologists with concrete positive discriminators (e.g., hypertelorism, scleral hue) while cementing normal lens stability on biomicroscopy as an expected finding in LDS6.

evidence.text: Loeys-Dietz syndrome multisystem involvement consistently features hypertelorism as part of the core triad along with arterial tortuosity/aneurysm and uvula/palate anomalies across TGFB2/3 and SMAD2/3 entities.

source.title: A mutation update on the LDS‐associated genes TGFB2/3 and SMAD2/3
source.quote: The Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) is a connective tissue disorder affecting the cardiovascular, skeletal, and ocular system. Most typically, LDS patients present with aortic aneurysms and arterial tortuosity, hypertelorism, and bifid/broad uvula or cleft palate.

new_directions.question_text: Across all published primary clinical descriptions of SMAD2 pathogenic variant carriers, did any individual receive a formal slit-lamp biomicroscopic examination confirming or excluding subclinical lens subluxation?
new_directions.rationale: Verifying whether ophthalmologic evaluations in SMAD2 probands specifically performed slit-lamp checks rather than gross inspection will resolve whether true ectopia lentis is definitively 0% or simply under-reported.

new_directions.question_text: In meta-analyses reporting ectopia lentis in LDS cohorts, which specific genetic subtypes (e.g., TGFBR1/2 vs SMAD2/3 vs TGFB2/3) accounted for the positive cases, and were those variants independently validated as causative?
new_directions.rationale: Deconstructing aggregate review data will demonstrate whether the documented ectopia lentis cases in LDS literature were erroneous clinical classifications prior to modern sequencing panels or genuine outliers.
